Hi Alice / CloudVision team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, we want to align on the commercial pathway and procurement flow for your GCP Marketplace listing so the launch and initial co-sell motion are smooth. Key goals for this thread:

- Map the buyer-facing purchase path (GKE/Compute SKUs, billing flow, entitlements)
- Confirm procurement milestones (PO, DocuSign SOW, billing account mapping)
- Agree on internal owners and timeline for seller enablement artifacts

I've looped in Kar (pricing & marketplace intake), Vanessa (ops & launch), and Priyom (partner sales cadence) to help drive requirements.

Proposed next steps:
1) CloudVision confirms target buyer procurement team + PO cadence
2) Redwood shares a seller enablement checklist and procurement matrix (attached)
3) We schedule a 30-min procurement alignment call next week to lock on DocuSign timelines and GCP SKU mapping

Attachments: seller-enablement-checklist.xlsx (draft), procurement-matrix.csv

Can you confirm who from procurement will own PO coordination and whether CloudVision requires a consolidated invoice vs direct GCP billing?

Thanks,

Monica Patel

Subject: Re: Commercial pathway & buyflow: CloudVision GCP listing enablement

Hi Monica —

Thanks — this looks great. Quick answers:
- Procurement lead: Mei Lin (meilin@cloudvision.ai), cc'ed procurement@ for formal threads.
- We prefer a consolidated invoice (one bill to CloudVision) rather than separate GCP line-item billing to multiple teams.
- PO cadence: we typically issue a PO within 5 business days after SOW sign-off; for marketplace purchases we need the SKU mapping and entitlement documentation up front for our internal procurement system.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports:
1) consolidated invoicing (yes/no)
2) an entitlement token model that maps marketplace purchase to our CloudVision account (we require an API-based entitlement callback)

Happy to get Mei on a call next week. Available Tues/Wed afternoon PST.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Cloud Partnerships
CloudVision Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice@cloudvision.ai>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial pathway & buyflow: CloudVision GCP listing enablement

Thanks Alice — quick clarifications from our side:

1) Consolidated invoicing: Redwood supports consolidated billing for marketplace purchases but there are two options depending on customer preference:
   - Option A: Redwood issues a single consolidated invoice to CloudVision (we act as the billing entity). This requires a commercial billing arrangement and monthly settlements.
   - Option B: Purchases flow through GCP’s billing and CloudVision receives a single line-item invoice from GCP (we provide SKU mapping and partner-managed subscriptions).

2) Entitlement model: We provide an entitlement callback API and can issue entitlement tokens bound to a buyer account. Implementation details: POST /entitlements with buyer_id, sku_id -> returns entitlement_token. We will share the API spec on the Drive link below.

Procurement matrix notes (from attached):
- SOW required for Dedicated Reserved Options and Professional Services; standard hosted consumption can be enabled via SKU mapping alone.
- PO -> DocuSign match: most customers attach the PO number to the DocuSign SOW before signing to avoid delays.
- For co-sell incentives, CloudVision will need a partner attribution ID (we'll provide partner_id and partner_rate card).

Attachment: procurement-matrix.csv (contains mapping for SKU -> product_id -> billing_type)

Action items (from Redwood):
- I will draft an entitlement API spec and sample payload by Monday.
- Vanessa will prepare a canonical SOW template for marketplace co-sell engagements.

Monica, I suggest Tuesday 12/14 1:00pm PST for the alignment call (works for our team). Alice/Mei, does that time work?

Thanks,
Kar
Senior Partner Ops
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: procurement-matrix.csv (csv)]

I've attached a SOW draft (SOW-draft-v2.pdf) with redlines for procurement to review. A few ops notes:
- Timeline: once SOW is finalized and PO is issued we need ~7 business days to map SKUs and enable testing in the GCP listing sandbox.
- Canary strategy: we recommend a staged enablement (internal alpha -> closed beta to select customers -> full listing).
- Entitlement testing: we need a sandbox buyer account and an API callback endpoint for entitlement validation.

Vanessa's checklist (ops):
- Create sandbox buyer account for CloudVision (redwood-sbx-cloudvision)
- Upload SKU mapping to GCP partner console
- Coordinate DocuSign envelope id with procurement@cloudvision.ai
- Schedule canary window: target Dec 21–23 for sandbox validation
